overall_assessment: This is a plausible but weakly validated pain point. The evidence base is thin—only 2 low-specificity sources, no quantified impact data, and no direct user testimony about time lost or revenue saved. The problem is real at a conceptual level (WhatsApp does have quality ratings and messaging limits) but the frequency, severity, and current workaround cost are all unknowns. The strongest angle is regulatory/compliance risk (account suspension), but SIG-003's single review doesn't demonstrate widespread concern. Without evidence that manual monitoring fails frequently or that BSP tools are insufficient, a SaaS solution addressing 'proactive alerts' risks building a nice-to-have widget rather than a must-have tool. I would recommend deeper validation: at minimum 5-8 interviews with growth/ops managers at WhatsApp-sending companies to measure actual incident frequency, current alerting coverage, and satisfaction with existing BSP tools.
